name.text: Using reduction formulae to find exact values

questiontext.text:
Consider the expression

\[ [[if test="is(fr=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left([[if test="is(fm=1)"]]180^\circ - {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=2)"]]180^\circ + {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=3)"]]360^\circ - {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]]\right). \]

(a) Use a reduction formula to find the exact value of this expression.

Give your answer in exact form, use sqrt() for a square root

\([[if test="is(fr=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left([[if test="is(fm=1)"]]180^\circ - {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=2)"]]180^\circ + {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=3)"]]360^\circ - {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]]\right) = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

We need the exact value of \([[if test="is(fr=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left([[if test="is(fm=1)"]]180^\circ - {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=2)"]]180^\circ + {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=3)"]]360^\circ - {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]]\right) = [[if test="is(fr=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]\tan[[/if]] {@ang@}^\circ\).

Step 1: find the quadrant. The angle \({@ang@}^\circ\) lies in Quadrant [[if test="is(quad=2)"]]II[[/if]][[if test="is(quad=3)"]]III[[/if]][[if test="is(quad=4)"]]IV[[/if]]. Its reference angle (the acute angle it makes with the \(x\)-axis) is \(\alpha = {@theta@}^\circ\).

Step 2: find the sign. By the CAST rule, [[if test="is(sg>0)"]][[if test="is(fr=1)"]]sine[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]cosine[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]tangent[[/if]] is positive in Quadrant [[if test="is(quad=2)"]]II[[/if]][[if test="is(quad=3)"]]III[[/if]][[if test="is(quad=4)"]]IV[[/if]][[else]][[if test="is(fr=1)"]]sine[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]cosine[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]tangent[[/if]] is negative in Quadrant [[if test="is(quad=2)"]]II[[/if]][[if test="is(quad=3)"]]III[[/if]][[if test="is(quad=4)"]]IV[[/if]][[/if]]. So the reduction formula is

\[ [[if test="is(fr=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left([[if test="is(fm=1)"]]180^\circ - \theta[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=2)"]]180^\circ + \theta[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=3)"]]360^\circ - \theta[[/if]]\right) = [[if test="is(sg<0)"]]-[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\,\theta, \qquad\text{so}\qquad [[if test="is(fr=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left([[if test="is(fm=1)"]]180^\circ - {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=2)"]]180^\circ + {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=3)"]]360^\circ - {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]]\right) = [[if test="is(sg<0)"]]-[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]\tan[[/if]] {@theta@}^\circ. \]

Step 3: use the exact value of the acute angle. From the special triangles, \([[if test="is(fr=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]\tan[[/if]] {@theta@}^\circ = {@bval@}\).

Final answer: \([[if test="is(fr=1)"]]\sin[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]\cos[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]\tan[[/if]]\left([[if test="is(fm=1)"]]180^\circ - {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=2)"]]180^\circ + {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]][[if test="is(fm=3)"]]360^\circ - {@theta@}^\circ[[/if]]\right) = {@ta1@}\).

questiondescription.text: Objective: use the reduction formulae for 180° − θ, 180° + θ and 360° − θ, with the CAST rule, to find exact values of sin, cos and tan.

truefeedback.text: Check the sign. The angle \({@ang@}^\circ\) is in Quadrant [[if test="is(quad=2)"]]II[[/if]][[if test="is(quad=3)"]]III[[/if]][[if test="is(quad=4)"]]IV[[/if]]; use the CAST rule to decide whether [[if test="is(fr=1)"]]sine[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]cosine[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]tangent[[/if]] is positive or negative there.

That is the value of a different ratio. A reduction formula keeps the same ratio: [[if test="is(fr=1)"]]sine[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]cosine[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]tangent[[/if]] of the angle becomes [[if test="is(fr=1)"]]sine[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=2)"]]cosine[[/if]][[if test="is(fr=3)"]]tangent[[/if]] of the reference angle.

falsefeedback.text: First find the quadrant and the reference angle, then use the CAST rule for the sign, and finally the special triangles for the exact value.
